extracted.intended_audience: American writers, critics, and literary reformers (aspiring literatuses and those shaping national literature)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance and evaluative criteria for composing and judging future American literature—qualities of the author, thematic aims, stylistic prescriptions, and social functions of literary works in a democratic nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character as primary requirement (not mere erudition or elegance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "character will be a main requirement, and not merely erudition or elegance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary worth is measured first by moral/psychic depth and authentic character rather than technical learning or ornamental style. Avoid works that are impressive only for scholarship or polish without substantive character or vigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intense and loving comradeship as a literary ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: "Intense and loving comradeship, the personal and passionate attachment of man to man...will then be fully express'd."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate themes of deep, loyal human friendship and camaraderie in manners and literature as a counterbalance to materialism; literature should make such bonds visible and formative for democratic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the covert, lurid, and Puritanical grimness
rubrics_metrics.description: "the absence in him of the idea of the covert, the lurid, the maleficent, the devil, the grim estimates inherited from the Puritans..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject morbid, lurid, or demonizing preoccupations inherited from puritanical sensibilities. Anti-patterns include dwelling on depravity, lurid sensationalism, or covert malign fantasies as a staple of artistic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial qualities: cheerful simplicity, natural standards, faith, reverence, absence of affectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The great literatus will be known...by his cheerful simplicity, his adherence to natural standards, his limitless faith in God, his reverence, and by the absence in him of doubt, ennui, burlesque, persiflage, or any strain'd and temporary fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should cultivate simplicity, reverence, faith (broadly conceived), and resist transient fashions, cynicism, or frivolous parody. Style and temperament should reflect naturalness and steady seriousness rather than irony or jadedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's highest aim: moral civilization (conscience, justice, truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature ... must be its moral civilization--the formulation, expression, and aidancy whereof, is the very highest height of literature...right, justice, truth...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foremost end of literature is to formulate and foster moral conscience and justice; works should ultimately radiate ethical purpose that helps elevate society beyond mere material achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance religion with science to prevent fanaticism
rubrics_metrics.description: "side by side with the unflagging stimulation of the elements of religion and conscience must henceforth move with equal sway, science, absolute reason...to prevent fanaticism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious or metaphysical themes must be paired with scientific reason and empirical understanding to avoid extreme credulity or fanaticism. Literary works should integrate rather than isolate spiritual fervor and rational inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore and represent true Nature (the kosmos) broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature, true Nature, and the true idea of Nature...must furnish the pervading atmosphere to poems...not the smooth walks, trimm'd hedges...but the whole orb, with its geologic history, the kosmos...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict Nature in its vast, geological, and cosmic dimensions—far beyond garden idylls. Use wide-ranging natural imagery (sky, air, land, geologic time) as the pervading atmosphere for high literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace Idealism; counter excessive realism
rubrics_metrics.description: The elevating and etherealizing ideas of the unknown and of unreality must be brought forward with authority...to confront the growing excess and arrogance of realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should confidently present ideal, spiritual, or 'unreal' elements as legitimate and necessary counterweights to the age's materialist realism. Do not capitulate entirely to the standards of empirical realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote health, joyousness, and an 'al fresco' spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong fibred joyousness and faith, and the sense of health al fresco, may well enter into the preparation of future noble American authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should convey wholesome vitality, outdoor health, and joyousness rather than morbidity. The sensibility of literature ought to reflect robust physical and mental life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-making and imaginative projection over mechanical reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the image-making faculty...No useless attempt to repeat the material creation, by daguerreotyping the exact likeness by mortal mental means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the creative faculty that projects analogies and transforms perceptions; avoid mere photographic, literal reproduction of external reality. The poet/artist should reimagine and synthesize rather than copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluative test: Does the book 'help any human soul'?
rubrics_metrics.description: "The true question to ask respecting a book, is, _has it help'd any human soul?_"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate standard of a great book is its ability to benefit, uplift, or aid a human soul. Artistic techniques matter, but works claiming first-class status must pass this humane test.

rubrics_metrics.name: First trial by art-qualities, then by ethical foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: All works of art are to be first tried by their art qualities...Then, whenever claiming to be first-class works, they are to be strictly and sternly tried by their foundation in, and radiation, in the highest sense, and always indirectly, of the ethic principles...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate literature first on formal/artistic merits (image-making, drama, sound, plot), and then judge whether it embodies and radiates ethical depth; both levels are necessary for first-class status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume an active reader; write suggestively (reader constructs the work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books are to be call'd for, and supplied, on the assumption that the process of reading is not a half-sleep...the reader is to do something for himself...the text furnishing the hints, the clue, the start or frame-work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose texts that require engagement and construction by the reader: hint, suggest, and provide a framework rather than over-explain. This fosters supple, intuitive minds and active reading practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create native American formulations rather than imitate Old-World models
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost everything that has been written...needs to be re-written, re-sung, re-stated, in terms consistent with the institution of these States...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce literature rooted in American conditions, characters, and democratic institutions. Recasting older European models into native terms is preferred over slavish imitation of foreign forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate fairness, manliness, decorum; strengthen self-suppliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A highest widest aim of democratic literature may well be to bring forth, cultivate, brace, and strengthen this sense [of fairness, manliness, decorum]...A strong mastership of the general inferior self by the superior self...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should nurture internal moral regulation—fairness, courage, decorum—and help citizens govern themselves ethically more than relying solely on laws or external enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce poets who reconcile science, spiritualism, and metaphysics (poems of death)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must ... appear poets...who will, now and ever, so link and tally the rational physical being of man, with the ensembles of time and space, and with this vast and multiform show, Nature...compose the great poem of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage poetry that integrates scientific understanding with spiritual inquiry—works that confront death and the beyond with both intellect and devotion, restoring faith informed by science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language style: energetic, suggestive, and nature-fanned (care for impetus and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: A language fann'd by the breath of Nature, which leaps overhead, cares mostly for impetus and effects, and for what it plants and invigorates to grow...seldomer tells a thing than suggests or necessitates it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a vigorous, evocative idiom that privileges momentum and evocative suggestion over exhaustive explanation. Favor language that invigorates and prompts growth in reader imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on inherited libraries and secondhand application
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigating here, we see, not that it is a little thing we have, in having the bequeath'd libraries...yet how serious the danger, depending entirely on them, of the bloodless vein, the nerveless arm, the false application, at second or third hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize original observation and lived experience over merely reusing past texts. Beware of derivative, bloodless writing that substitutes secondhand erudition for fresh perception and vigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim ultimately at metaphysics and spiritual mysteries; literature's altitude is religion
rubrics_metrics.description: The culmination and fruit of literary artistic expression...are in metaphysics, including the mysteries of the spiritual world...The altitude of literature and poetry has always been religion--and always will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize metaphysical inquiry and spiritual themes as among the highest aims of literature; works addressing the immortal, the soul, and ultimate questions secure lasting human value even if stylistically imperfect.
